list that member's transaction ids by hand.

AlbionDataMarketPrice.description:
Current market values returned by Albion Online Data.

Uses optional timestamps because the upstream emits empty strings when no order is available for
a city/quality pair. Keeping those rows lets the UI distinguish "no order" from "row missing".

# Example
```rust,ignore
# use backend::modules::albiondata::client::AlbionDataMarketPrice;
let price = AlbionDataMarketPrice {
    item_id: "T4_BAG".to_string(),
    city: "Caerleon".to_string(),
    quality: 1,
    sell_price_min: 1200,
    sell_price_min_date: None,
    sell_price_max: 1400,
    sell_price_max_date: None,
    buy_price_min: 900,
    buy_price_min_date: None,
    buy_price_max: 1000,
    buy_price_max_date: None,
};
assert_eq!(price.item_id, "T4_BAG");
```

game's table gives a different reduction for melee, ranged and mounted attackers.

baseline_value.description:
The comparison value for a period-over-period rule. `None` for a
threshold-only rule.

`attention::rules`'s function names.

sample_size.description:
The sample size the rule's minimum-sample gate was evaluated
against.

subject_type.description:

(`subject_id` is then `None`), or `"enemy_guild"` for a
per-enemy-guild rule such as `stale_intel`.

BackfillOutcome.description:
One page of a manually-triggered scouting backfill, older than
`before` and bounded by `limit`. Unlike `scout_recent_snapshots`
(which always looks at the newest snapshots), this is a cursor an
officer pages backward through history with: call once, then call
again passing `oldest_considered_start_time` from the response as the
next call's `before`, until `considered` is 0.

considered.description:
How many snapshots this call looked at, before the already-scouted
skip. `0` means the cursor has reached the end of history.

oldest_considered_start_time.description:
The earliest `start_time` among the snapshots this call considered.
`None` when `considered` is `0`. Pass this back as the next call's
`before` to keep paging backward.

scouted.description: How many of the considered snapshots were newly scouted.

event was picked up by the background sync and cannot be attributed to

BattleDetail.description: Full battle detail, extending the summary with per-player and kill timeline.

BattleEconomyView.description:
Trade-and-cost view for `GET /api/economy/battles/{battle_id}`: one
`battle_loss_estimates` row, verbatim, plus a derived comparison field.

battle_id.description: Canonical `AlbionBB` battle id this estimate covers.

enemy_estimated_loss.description:
Silver value of the enemy side's priced victim equipment. **This is a
trade indicator only, never income.** It exists so an officer can see
"did we come out ahead in the silver trade", not "how much did we
earn" — this module's income is declared via `splits`, never inferred
from combat.

enemy_priced_items.description: How many of the enemy side's victim item stacks actually got a market price.

enemy_total_items.description:
How many of the enemy side's victim item stacks existed at all — the
denominator for a coverage percentage
(`enemy_priced_items / enemy_total_items`).

friendly_estimated_loss.description:
Silver value of our side's priced victim equipment. A cost figure —
never income.

friendly_priced_items.description: How many of our side's victim item stacks actually got a market price.

friendly_total_items.description:
How many of our side's victim item stacks existed at all — the
denominator for a coverage percentage
(`friendly_priced_items / friendly_total_items`).

priced_at.description:
RFC 3339. When this estimate was computed — the reproducibility
anchor, since market prices drift.

pricing_location.description: The city/market location this estimate was priced against.

trade_net.description:
`enemy_estimated_loss - friendly_estimated_loss`. Positive means the
enemy lost more silver than we did in this battle; negative means we
came out behind in the trade. **This is a trade comparison, not a
profit figure** — it is never money that moved, and never enters any
income/revenue total.

This battle segment's canonical Fight outcome: `"victory"`, `"defeat"`, `"draw"`, or
`"unknown"` when the segment has no linked Fight yet.

This is a **Fight-level** verdict, not a per-segment one: `AlbionBB` can split one real
engagement into several battle segments, and every segment belonging to the same
multi-segment Fight reports the same value here on purpose — they are the same
engagement. Previously this field was `is_win: bool`; that type could not honestly

changed shape instead of just swapping its source column.

EventEconomyView.description:
The real P&L view for `GET /api/economy/events/{event_id}`.

Every income figure here comes from the real ledger (`splits`,
`regear_deaths`) — never from a combat estimate. See the module doc
comment above and `modules::economy`'s own doc comment for the rule this
answers to.

Sum of `battle_loss_estimates.friendly_estimated_loss` across every
battle belonging to any fight attached to this event. Informational
context only — how costly the fighting was, regardless of whether it
got reimbursed. Never subtracted into `net`.

income_total.description:
`SUM(splits.net_value)` for this event's splits with
`status = "completed"` — the only split status whose `net_value`
represents real, realized income. Deliberately excludes
`siphoned_energy_entries` (it carries no `event_id`, and attributing
one to a specific event would require an unreliable timestamp-overlap
guess); the guild-wide `GET /api/intel/report` already covers siphoned
energy in its own broader weekly view, this endpoint is deliberately
event-scoped and narrower.

net.description:
`income_total - regear_paid_total`. **The only real money-movement
figure.** Deliberately does NOT subtract `friendly_combat_loss_total`:
a loss that got paid out is already reflected in `regear_paid_total`,
and a loss that never got a regear request was never guild money in
the first place — subtracting it again would double-count.

regear_coverage_pct.description:
`regear_paid_total / friendly_combat_loss_total * 100.0` — what
fraction of our actual combat losses the guild ended up reimbursing.
`None` when `friendly_combat_loss_total` is `0` (never divides by zero).

regear_paid_total.description:
`SUM(regear_deaths.final_amount)` for this event's regear deaths with
`status = "approved"` — the only state where a regear was actually
paid out of the bank.

regear_requested_total.description:
`SUM(regear_deaths.auto_estimate_total)` across EVERY regear death row
for this event, regardless of status — every death ever logged as
regear-eligible, whether or not it was ultimately paid. Purely
informational context (see `regear_coverage_pct`); never summed into `net`.

OpenAlbionItemAbilities.description:
Every ability an item family offers, grouped by the slot that can hold it.

Keyed in the bundled dataset by the tier-stripped base identifier (`MAIN_SWORD`), because all
eight tiers of one item offer the same spells.

`active` and `passive` map a slot index (as a string, `"1"`, `"2"`, `"3"`) to the choices that
slot accepts. Active slot 1/2/3 are the player's Q/W/E on a weapon; armor pieces have a single
active slot bound to D (head), R (chest) or F (shoes). An item with zero slots of a kind — an
off-hand, a cape — carries an empty map, and the UI shows no picker for it.

resource.description: First segment of the key, used to group the matrix (`bank`, `regear`, …).

available_permissions.description:
Every permission the backend can gate on, so the UI can render the
full grid rather than only what happens to be granted today.

permission_catalog.description: Same keys as `available_permissions`, with resource/action split for grouping.

roles.description: Every role known to the system, highest priority first.

user_id.description: The member placed there.

PlannedFightParticipantView.description: An event roster member planned for this fight's linked event.

albion_player_id.description: Linked Albion character ID used for observation matching, if the user has linked one.

observed.description: Whether this planned participant was observed in a persisted friendly snapshot.

primary_build_id.description: `None` when the participant selected the virtual Fill role.

user_id.description: Internal event participant user ID.

entry_count.description: Total number of ledger rows contributing to this aggregate.

first_seen.description: RFC3339 timestamp of the earliest row for this player.

last_seen.description: RFC3339 timestamp of the latest row for this player.

net.description: Net ledger balance. A deposit → withdrawal → redeposit cycle counts only its current balance.

player_name.description:
The Albion player name. Uses the casing of the most recent row for that player so the
client renders the "current" spelling.

total_deposited.description: Current positive balance after netting deposits against withdrawals. Always >= 0.

total_withdrawn.description: Current debt/negative balance after netting deposits against withdrawals. Always >= 0.

recent_entries.description: The most recent entries for this player (default 20, capped by the service).

PlayerLossEstimate.description: Per-player loss estimate for one battle.

PlayerReport.description:
One member's combat record, isolated from the guild report.

`member` carries every total the guild report's roster table already
shows for this user (fights, silver, splits, siphoned, fill rate); `weekly`
and `recent_fights` are the two things a single roster row cannot show —
how those totals built up over the window, and the individual fights
behind them.

recent_fights.description:
This member's fights, newest first, capped at
[`PLAYER_RECENT_FIGHTS_LIMIT`].

weekly.description:
One entry per week in the window, oldest first, zero-filled gaps
included — same convention as [`GuildReport::trends`].

win_streak.description: Consecutive wins counting back from the most recent fight.

PlayerTrendBucket.description:
One member's activity in a single week, the per-player counterpart to
[`TrendBucket`].

Unlike the guild-wide bucket this carries `win_rate` directly rather than
leaving the caller to divide `wins` by `wins + losses`: a single player's
week is thin enough (often 0-3 fights) that "no fights" and "0% win rate"
need to stay visibly different, which a client-side division would blur.

week_start.description: Monday 00:00 UTC of this week, RFC 3339.

Preference.description: Which build a member already asked to fly, if any — a signal to prefer, not a constraint.

ProblemDetails.description: The standard RFC 7807 Problem Details representation for HTTP API errors.

code.description: Stable machine-readable error code (additive; absent on legacy problems).

detail.description: A human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence of the problem.

instance.description: A URI reference that identifies the specific occurrence of the problem.

invalid_params.description: Optional parameter validation errors or specific metadata.

oneOf.description: Where the authoritative entity lives, set when a write hit a read-only copy.

status.description: The HTTP status code generated by the origin server for this occurrence.

title.description: A short, human-readable summary of the problem type.

type.description: A URI reference that identifies the problem type.

ProgressionMeView.description: The caller's (or a target user's) season XP snapshot.

oneOf.description: Configured progression tier for the current season XP (never a permission).

level.description: Current level in that season (1 when there is no account row).

lifetime_xp.description: Sum of XP across every season this user has an account in.

next_level_at.description: Cumulative threshold of the next level (`0` at cap).

rank.description: 1-based rank in the season by XP, `None` if no season.

oneOf.description: Active season covering `now`, if any.

xp_to_next.description: XP still needed for the next level (`0` at cap or with no season).

ProgressionSettingsView.description: Guild-wide progression knobs plus a short curve preview.

guild_ranks.description: Ordered progression tiers. Discord mappings never trigger role mutations.

level_preview.description: First 20 (or `max_level`) thresholds for the admin preview table.

message_channel_deny_list.description: Channel ids that never grant message XP.

message_cooldown_secs.description: Minimum seconds between message awards for one user.

message_min_chars.description: Minimum message length for message XP.

vod_forum_channel_id.description: Discord forum channel id for VOD threads.

warn_threshold.description: Active-warn count that opens an admin escalation.

xp_event_complete.description: XP for still being on the roster at event stop.

PutTenantFeaturesRequest.description: PUT payload for a tenant's flags.

flags.description: Desired flag states. Missing keys are left unchanged.

updated.description: How many rows flipped from unread to read.

ReadinessObservation.description:
What Item Power the roster that actually fought an event turned out to have, versus what
[`super::readiness::evaluate`] predicted for it beforehand.

avg_item_power.description:
Simple average of `fight_stats.avg_friendly_item_power` across those fights — one fight,
one vote, unweighted by player count, matching the same per-fight-averaging convention
`attention::rules::evaluate_ip_deficit` already uses for exactly this kind of cross-fight
IP averaging.

fight_count.description: Distinct fights this event has a `fight_stats` rollup for.

item_power_delta.description:
`avg_item_power - predicted.avg_item_power_now`. Positive means the roster that actually
fought brought more Item Power than the pre-event prediction; negative means less.

thread_id.description: Discord thread snowflake created for the VOD post.

bonus_balance.description: Requests currently available from the bonus pool (giveaway-earned).

weekly_balance.description: Requests currently available from the weekly pool.

RegearItemOverride.description: One slot's item, replacing the chosen build's canonical item for this request only.

openalbion_item_enchantment.description: Albion enchantment level (`0..=4`) of the replacement item.

openalbion_item_id.description: The `OpenAlbion` catalog id of the replacement item.

openalbion_item_quality.description: Albion quality (`1..=5`) of the replacement item.

RegearSettingsView.description: Guild-wide regear settings, as seen by the client.

bonus_request_cap.description: The bonus pool (giveaway-earned) never accumulates past this cap.

enabled_slots_mask.description: Bitmask over `BuildSlot` deciding which slots are reimbursable.

pricing_location.description: Albion city whose market prices are used for estimates.

weekly_request_cap.description: The weekly pool never accumulates past this cap.

weekly_request_topup_amount.description: How many requests are added to a user's weekly pool each elapsed week.

RegearSource.description:
Where a regear death row came from.

Stored in the database as its lowercase string form, same convention as [`RegearStatus`].
Officers and members can tell the two apart in the UI, but the accept/reject workflow never
branches on it — both origins are just `regear_deaths` rows once inserted.

RegearStatus.description: The lifecycle status of a regear death row.

ign.description: In-game name to resolve via Albion search. Must match exactly one player.

albion_alliance_id.description: Albion alliance id. Required when `kind` is `alliance`.

albion_allied_guild_ids.description: Optional comma-separated allied Albion guild ids.

albion_allied_guild_names.description: Optional comma-separated allied Albion guild names.

albion_api_region.description: Albion gameinfo region: `europe`, `americas`, or `asia`. Required for `kind=guild`.

albion_guild_id.description: Albion Online guild id to pull roster/battles from. Required for `kind=guild`; omit for alliance.

member_guild_ids.description: Guild tenant ids to invite when registering an alliance.

RegisterableGuild.description: A Discord guild the user may register as a tenant.

can_manage.description:
Whether this Discord user owns the guild or holds `Manage Server` /
`Administrator` in it.

Computed once at login from the OAuth `guilds` scope and carried in the
signed `registerable_guilds` cookie, so `POST /api/tenants/register`
can check it as a fast path with no Discord round trip. It is a cache,
not the only guard: that handler also re-verifies live via the bot
token when this is stale, absent, or `false`, so a session older than
the cookie's lifetime — or a brand-new server the bot just joined —
still registers correctly. See [`DiscordGuild::can_manage`].

RejectRegearRequest.description: Request body for officer reject. The note is mandatory.

note.description: Why the request was rejected. 1..=500 chars.

RejectWithdrawalRequest.description: Request body for an officer to reject requested withdrawals.

all.description:
If `true`, reject every currently-requested transaction guild-wide (across all members)
instead of listing `transaction_ids` individually.

guild_tenant_id.description: Member guild whose ledger to mutate when the current tenant is an alliance.

transaction_ids.description:
The specific transaction ids to reject. Each must currently be `requested`. Omit this and
set `all: true` instead to reject everything at once.

user_id.description:
Restrict `all` to a single member.

Without it `all: true` sweeps the whole guild, which is the wrong tool
when an officer wants to settle up with one person: they would have to
list that member's transaction ids by hand.

ReportDataQuality.description: Caveats that explain gaps in the numbers above.

unlinked_players.description: Albion characters seen in battle that map to no linked member.

ReportEconomy.description:
Silver in and out.

Regear and split figures are **breakdowns of** `outflow_total`, not addends
to it. See [`compute_economy`] for why that distinction matters.

fame_per_million_lost.description: Kill fame earned per million silver lost.

guild_treasury_net.description: Guild treasury net balance from splits and regears (`split_tax_total + bank_donated - regear_paid - outflow_other`).

split_bags_total.description: Silver bags (`bags_value`) across completed splits in window.

split_net_distributed.description: Net silver distributed to participants after repairs and guild tax.

split_tax_total.description: Guild tax retained across completed splits in window.

attendance.description: Total signups across events in range.

inactive_members.description: Members with no signups in the window.

regear_weekly_cap.description: Weekly regear request-pool cap currently configured.

role_need.description: Seats each role was asked for, from comp build quantities.

slots.description: Total seats those events called for.

unlinked.description: Members with no linked Albion character.

attributed_fights.description: Fights that could be attributed to one of our comps via an event.

item_power_delta.description: Our average item power minus theirs; negative means we field lighter.

win_streak.description: Consecutive wins counting back from the most recent fight.

ResolvedAttributeChange.description: One resolved damage or healing line, after every multiplier.

base_change.description: The spell's baseline `change`, before any multiplier here.

resolved_change.description:
`base_change` after area escalation, focus fire (damage to `Enemy` only) and the zerg

`cast_at + hit_delay` — when the effect actually lands, and the order casts are processed
in.

per_target_health_change.description:
The resolved change applied to *each* named target — not a pooled total. A cast naming
three targets deals this figure to every one of them.

prior_cc_stacks.description:
How many earlier same-kind crowd-control applications on this cast's targets were found
within the diminishing-returns decay window.

resolved_time.description: `base_time` after area escalation, the zerg debuff and crowd-control diminishing returns.

confirm_no_post.description: Operator confirmed that all bot workers are stopped and no post exists.

grants_staff.description: Holders also receive the generic staff Discord role.

is_staff.description: Unique generic staff ping role linked to the Discord role used for `@staff`.

permissions.description: Permission keys granted to this role.

priority.description: Ordering weight; higher wins when a member holds several roles.

role_id.description: Internal primary key of `roles` (UUID for newly created rows).

RunSummary.description: One pinned run of a scenario version, for list views.

versions.description: Every version sharing this scenario's name, oldest first.

casts.description: One entry per cast that resolved, ordered by `land_at`.

Fraction of `total_damage_dealt` that landed on a target already at `0` hit points —

unknown_spells.description: Casts whose `spell_id` is not in the bundled dataset at all.

guild_id.description: Restrict to one opponent guild id.

q.description: Free-text match on scout name or opponent guild name.

ScoutOutcome.description: The result of scouting a battle, before or after persistence.

already_linked.description: Whether the battle was already linked to this scout.

merged.description: Whether this merged into an existing scout rather than creating one.

scouted_comp_id.description: Scout id, absent for a dry run.

matchup_coverage.description: How much of the underlying battle data could be attributed to a comp.

`None` means we have never fought this opponent with a comp we can

`max_item_power - best_candidate_item_power`: the Item Power a training push could still

info.description:
# Weaklings Gateway API

Backend REST API for the Weaklings guild management app: Discord OAuth2 login, a database-backed Guild Bank ledger, loot splits, and Albion Online integrations. This description is the map — read it once before touching any endpoint below.

## Base URL and routing

Every path documented here is already prefixed with `/api` (e.g. the `auth` tag's login endpoint is served at `/api/auth/discord/login`). The frontend should never need any other prefix.

## Authentication: it's a cookie, not a bearer token

There is no `Authorization` header and no JWT. Login is a server-side Discord OAuth2 redirect flow:

1. Send the browser to `GET /api/auth/discord/login`. It redirects to Discord, which redirects back to `GET /api/auth/discord/callback` on this server.
2. The callback exchanges the code, resolves the user's Discord guild roles against the local `roles` table, upserts a local `users` row, and sets an **httponly** `session_user` cookie (7-day expiry) containing the serialized profile — the frontend never reads or parses this cookie directly.
3. The server then redirects the browser to the frontend's `/dashboard`.
4. From then on, the browser sends the cookie automatically on every same-site request. Call `GET /api/auth/me` on app load to check whether a session exists and to get the logged-in user's profile (id, username, avatar, roles). A `401` means "not logged in" — show the login button.
5. `POST /api/auth/logout` revokes the session server-side and clears the cookie; `POST /api/auth/logout-all` revokes every session of the caller's account.

Every endpoint below other than the four `auth` ones requires this cookie to already be set; they are all annotated with the `session_cookie` security requirement. Because it's a cookie, `fetch()` calls from the frontend need `credentials: "include"` (or same-origin, if proxied).

## Roles and authorization

Authorization is **permission-based**: each protected endpoint declares a fine-grained
`Permission` (e.g. `bank.withdraw.accept`, `splits.manage`) via a `Require(...)` extractor,
and the request is rejected with `403` if the caller's roles don't grant it.

The mapping **role → permission** lives in the `role_permissions` database table and is
loaded into an in-memory cache at startup. To change who can do what:

1. Create a gestionale role with `POST /api/admin/roles` and link it to a Discord snowflake.
2. Grant or revoke keys on that role with `PUT /api/admin/roles/{id}/permissions` (applies immediately).
3. `POST /api/admin/permissions/reload` still exists for out-of-band SQL edits.

The configured `super_admin_discord_id` (env) bypasses every permission check.

Current permissions:

| Permission               | Granted to        | Used by                                    |
|--------------------------|-------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| `bank.withdraw.accept`   | Admin, Officer    | `POST /bank/transactions/withdraw/accept`  |
| `bank.view_others`       | Admin             | `GET /bank/balance?user_id=`, `GET /bank/transactions?user_id=` |
| `splits.manage`          | Admin, Officer    | split edit/close endpoints                 |
| `splits.islands.manage`  | Admin             | island/tab catalog CRUD                    |
| `users.create`           | Admin             | `POST /users`, `GET /admin/discord/members` |
| `permissions.reload`     | Admin             | `POST /admin/permissions/reload`           |
| `roles.manage`           | Admin             | `POST/PATCH/DELETE /admin/roles`           |
| `comps.build_categories.manage` | Admin, Officer | build category CRUD endpoints |
| `comps.comp_categories.manage` | Admin, Officer | comp category CRUD endpoints |
| `comps.builds.manage`    | Admin, Officer    | edit/delete/archive/version any build (create/edit/delete alone: own builds only) |
| `comps.comps.manage`     | Admin, Officer    | edit/delete/archive/version any comp (create/edit/delete alone: own comps only) |

A `403 Forbidden` (`ProblemDetails`) means the session is valid but the caller's roles don't
grant the required permission.

## Response envelope

Every successful (2xx) JSON response — except the two endpoints that stream a raw array or object directly (`openalbion` weapon stats/categories) — is wrapped JSend-style:

```json
{ "status": "success", "data": { /* the documented body schema */ } }
```

Always read the payload from `.data`, not the top level.

## Error format (RFC 7807)

Every non-2xx response is `application/problem+json`:

```json
{
  "type": "/errors/validation-error",
  "title": "Validation Error",
  "status": 400,
  "detail": "human-readable explanation, safe to show the user"
}
```

Common `status`/`type` pairs you'll see across this API: `400` validation-error, `401` unauthorized (no/invalid session), `403` forbidden (valid session, wrong role, or acting on someone else's resource), `404` not-found, `409` conflict (e.g. an Albion player already linked to another account), `502` upstream-service-error (a third-party API — Albion Online or OpenAlbion — failed or timed out).

## The two-step Guild Bank withdrawal flow

Money owed to a member never gets marked paid in one step. `bank.TransactionStatus` moves strictly forward: `pending` (owed, untouched) -> `requested` (the member asked to withdraw it, via `POST /bank/transactions/withdraw`) -> `withdrawn` (an officer accepted and paid it, via `POST /bank/transactions/withdraw/accept`, which stamps that officer's user id onto the transaction's `from_user_id` as the recorded payer). `GET /bank/balance` reports `pending_total`/`pending_count` and `requested_total`/`requested_count` separately so the UI can distinguish "owed" from "already asked for, awaiting payout".

## The loot split lifecycle

A split is requested by any member together with its participants and their relative weights up front (`POST /splits` — there is no separate "add participants later" step required to make a split valid, though `POST /splits/{id}/participants` still exists for an officer to adjust the roster while it's pending). `splits.SplitStatus` starts at `pending` and an officer closes it out exactly once, into one of three terminal-ish states: `completed` (`POST /splits/{id}/complete` — computes `net_value = estimated_market_value - repair_value + bags_value` and generates one `pending` Guild Bank transaction per participant, split proportionally by weight with remainder correction so the sum is exact), `not_completed` (the split didn't happen; no transactions), or `lost` (`POST /splits/{id}/lost` — the loot itself was never recovered; no transactions). Only `pending` splits can be edited or closed; every closing action is a one-way door.

## Albion Online vs. OpenAlbion — two unrelated third-party integrations

Don't confuse these tags: `albion` calls Sandbox Interactive's own (unofficial, undocumented) `gameinfo` API — live player/guild data for the configured in-game guild, plus the Discord-account-to- Albion-character self-link feature. `openalbion` calls the separate, community-run OpenAlbion item database — static reference data (weapon catalog, categories, per-quality stats) used by the composition/loadout builder, with the full weapon list cached server-side for an hour. Neither requires or shares any credentials; both simply require a valid session cookie like everything else.

For alliance-owned event splits, the complete participant roster is preflighted against stored event guild attributions and active alliance memberships before any destination ledger is written; valid shares are projected into the respective member-guild ledgers. Cross-tenant writes use a durable idempotent batch, so retry this endpoint after a transient failure to resume without duplicate credits. If a represented guild has left, the whole batch is blocked; remove its participants manually from the alliance split and retry. The one split-closing action that has a side effect beyond the split row itself: computes `net_value = estimated_market_value - repair_value + bags_value` (must be strictly positive), then creates one **new**, `pending`-status Guild Bank transaction per participant (`type = "split_credit"`, linked back via `split_id`), splitting `net_value` proportionally by weight with remainder correction on the last participant so the amounts sum exactly. Those transactions then follow the normal two-step withdrawal flow (`bank` tag) independently of this split. No request body. One-way door: only callable while `pending`; fails with `400` if there are no participants or if it's already `completed`/`not_completed`/`lost`. Requires the Admin or Officer role.
